title: Right Triangles
summary: Given a 2D boolean matrix, count the number of right triangles formed by three 1s where one element is in the same row as another and in the same column as the third, without being adjacent.
statement: Given a 2D boolean matrix, count the number of right triangles formed by three 1s where one element is in the same row as another and in the same column as the third, without being adjacent.
constraints: grid is a nonempty rectangular binary matrix.
Choose three one-cells forming a right angle whose legs follow one shared row and one shared column; distances may be any positive amount.
Count distinct triangles, with the right-angle cell distinguishing each choice.
hints: For each one-cell pivot, any other one in its row can pair with any other one in its column.
Precompute row and column one-counts, then sum (rowCount-1)*(columnCount-1) over one-cells.
Count rows and columns; for each grid[r][c]=1 add (rows[r]-1)(cols[c]-1).
Each factor independently chooses one endpoint, and every axis-aligned right triangle has exactly one right-angle pivot.
editorial: Each factor independently chooses one endpoint, and every axis-aligned right triangle has exactly one right-angle pivot.

tests.explanation: The center one can pair with the right one and either vertical one, producing two triangles.
Every corner can serve as the right-angle vertex, producing four triangles.
